item.title: With Midterms Approaching, Trump Implores Republicans: Pretend I’m on the Ballot!
item.description: President Trump was in South Carolina to stump for Darline Graham, sister of Lindsey. But his own political future was on his mind, too.
item.dc:creator: Shawn McCreesh
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump appeared at a rally with Senator Darline Graham ahead of the South Carolina Senate runoff.

item.title: Postal Service Publishes Finalized Plan to Restrict Mail Ballots
item.description: The plan complies with President Trump’s executive order to restrict mail voting, which was blocked by federal courts and is under review at the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Adam Sella
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A worker sorting ballots in 2025.

item.title: Judge Strikes Down Trump’s 75-Country Visa Ban
item.description: The ruling from the Southern District of New York found that the policy went beyond Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s legal authority.
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:credit: Anna Watts for The New York Times
item.media:description: Travelers arriving from international flights outside the U.S. Customs and Border Protection exit at Kennedy International Airport in New York last year.

item.title: Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to Illnesses in 15 States, F.D.A. Says
item.description: Officials are investigating after multiple strains of E. coli and a type of salmonella sickened dozens of people across the United States. Two people were infected with both salmonella and E. coli.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: St Petersburg Times/Zuma Press Wire, via Reuters
item.media:description: Public health officials have tied a number of salmonella and E. coli cases to alfalfa sprouts produced by a company in Minnesota.

item.title: Trump Accounts Get an Unlikely Endorser: Gavin Newsom
item.description: Mr. Newsom, the governor of California, normally has harsh words for President Trump. But he called the new children’s savings accounts “one of the best things” the president has done.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:credit: Jeff Chiu/Associated Press
item.media:description: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California gave an unusual endorsement for an endeavor led by President Trump — investment funds for American children born during Mr. Trump’s presidency.

item.title: Drawing on His Rust Belt Roots, Vance Campaigns for Republicans
item.description: Vice President JD Vance traveled to his hometown, Middletown, Ohio, and spoke at a steel factory where his grandfather once worked.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:credit: Jon Cherry/Associated Press
item.media:description: Vice President JD Vance spoke at a factory in Middletown, Ohio, on Friday.

item.title: Pentagon Fires Editor and Publisher of Independent Military Publication
item.description: The firings at Stars and Stripes also claimed a Middle East correspondent. They are the latest effort by the Pentagon to diminish the news outlet’s editorial independence.
item.dc:creator: Minho Kim
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Mark Godfrey/Associated Press
item.media:description: Service members reading Stars and Stripes in Cu Chi, South Vietnam, in September 1969. The publication has a long history of independent reporting on the U.S. military.

item.title: Defense Rests Case in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
item.description: The two sides focused Friday on whether Ms. Clancy was experiencing psychosis when she strangled her three young children in 2023. Closing arguments could begin on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao and Emma Schartz
item.media:credit: Josh Reynolds/Associated Press
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy in the courtroom on Thursday.

item.title: Court Slashes Award Alex Jones Was Ordered to Pay Sandy Hook Parents
item.description: An appeals court reduced the award to the parents of one victim to $6 million from $49 million, citing a Texas damages cap. The conspiracy theorist owes over $1 billion in other cases.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Williamson
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: For years, Alex Jones spread conspiracy theories that the Sandy Hook shooting was a hoax perpetrated by the government and the victims’ families.

item.title: America Ends a Summer of Lightning-Fast Primaries and Political Speed Dating
item.description: Plot twists in several states have led to rapid-fire races that have felt more reminiscent of European-style snap campaigns than traditional American marathons.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:credit: Meg Kinnard/Associated Press
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham and Representative Ralph Norman of South Carolina

item.title: Massachusetts’ Top Court Bars Statues of Catholic Saints at City Building
item.description: The ruling quashes a plan by the mayor of Quincy that had drawn opposition from many religious figures, as well as from residents of the racially diverse city.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: The mayor of Quincy had commissioned statues of St. Michael the Archangel and St. Florian in 2023 as the finishing touch for the city’s new public safety complex.

item.title: U.S. Agreed to Pay Liberia $5 Million in Connection with Deportees, Documents Say
item.description: The Trump administration approved the payment after Liberia said it would consider taking migrants from other countries.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo, Hamed Aleaziz and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:credit: Matthew Jacobs/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A plane carrying deportees from the United States at Roberts International Airport in Liberia on Thursday.

item.title: Desperation Mounts as Thousands in Indiana Endure 10 Days Without Power
item.description: Floods from powerful thunderstorms devastated Gary, where a third of residents live below the poverty line and full restoration isn’t expected until next week.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman and Robert Chiarito
item.media:credit: Octavio Jones/Reuters
item.media:description: Dinky Austin called the utility company for updates while she cooled off with ice outside of her home in Gary this week.

item.title: Small Plane Crashes in Western Alaska, Killing Eight
item.description: The Cessna aircraft was carrying two pilots, two U.S. Army engineers and four contractors to Cape Newenham from Anchorage when it crashed near a U.S. military site, investigators said.
item.dc:creator: Qasim Nauman, John Yoon and Alena Cerro
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: A Cessna 441 had taken off from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport and was headed to Cape Newenham, in Western Alaska, when it crashed around 11:45 a.m. Thursday, officials said.

item.title: Prison Firm Donated to Trump’s PAC After ICE Gave It $165 Million a Year in Contracts
item.description: The GEO Group has profited from the administration’s mass deportation campaign. A subsidiary donated more than $1.4 million to the president’s super PAC last month.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth P. Vogel and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Cornell Watson for The New York Times
item.media:description: The GEO Group signed a five-year contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement to operate a detention facility in Winton, N.C.

item.title: Chief Justice Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction, for Now
item.description: The 90,000-square-foot ballroom project has grown in size and scope, with the president’s lawyers saying it is intertwined with the renovation of an underground military bunker.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: The construction site for the new White House ballroom in March.

item.title: The Local: Drama in the Boundary Waters
item.description: William Kent Krueger talks about his thriller set in the Boundary Waters, a timely subject.
item.dc:creator: Jay Gabler

item.title: Guide Company That Ran Fatal Ski Trip Faces Safety Fine in California
item.description: The state levied a $151,300 fine on Blackbird Mountain Guides, which took backcountry skiers into the Sierra Nevada in threatening conditions. Nine died in an avalanche.
item.dc:creator: Dave Philipps
item.category: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
item.media:credit: Max Whittaker for The New York Times
item.media:description: A vigil in Truckee, Calif., for the victims of the Sierra Nevada avalanche.

item.title: Gazebos From Uzbekistan: The Latest Foreign Gifts in Trump’s Washington
item.description: The structures will go up in West Potomac Park, the site of President Trump’s planned National Garden of American Heroes.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Andrew Leyden for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers moving materials for Uzbek gazebos at West Potomac Park on Tuesday. President Trump’s expansive plans for the area also include reflecting pools, dining facilities and an amphitheater.

item.title: Trump Threatens Defamation Suit Over National Guard Report, Aiming to Intimidate a Critic
item.description: It was the latest example of President Trump’s bid to use the legal system against those who voice unflattering facts and opinions generally protected by the First Amendment.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: A report by the Center for American Progress determined that there was “no evidence” that President Trump’s deployment of the National Guard to cities across the country had affected the crime rate.

item.title: Push for Online Gun Sales Meets a Surprising Opponent: Small Gun Dealers
item.description: The Trump administration wants average Americans to be able to buy guns online and have them shipped to their doors. Small gun stores warn it could upend the industry and risk public safety.
item.dc:creator: Aishvarya Kavi
item.category: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Colin Overbey, the manager for Dunn’s Attic in Ormond Beach, Fla., is one of hundreds of people lobbying the A.T.F. to halt proposals that could alter the gun industry.

item.title: U.S. Citizen Who Deleted Phone’s Data Says His Prosecution Puts Privacy at Risk
item.description: Samuel Tunick, who faces a felony charge for deleting his phone’s data during an airport customs search, called the government’s peering into people’s private lives “creepy.”
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan
item.media:credit: Samuel Tunick
item.media:description: Samuel Tunick faces a felony charge for deleting his phone’s data during an airport customs search last year.

item.title: How Harvard’s Epic Fight With Trump Is Costing the University
item.description: The federal government has slowed Harvard’s funding, despite the university’s legal victories. The conflict is forcing hard choices on campus.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault and Irena Hwang
item.media:credit: Lucy Lu for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Trump administration has found new ways of trying to pressure Harvard to comply with its wishes.
